[Donald Trump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump "Donald Trump") , the 45th and 47th [president of the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_United_States "President of the United States") , made 19 international trips to 25 countries (in addition to visiting the [West Bank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Bank "West Bank") ) during [his first presidency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_presidency_of_Donald_Trump "First presidency of Donald Trump") , which began on [January 20, 2017](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_inauguration_of_Donald_Trump "First inauguration of Donald Trump") , and ended on [January 20, 2021](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inauguration_of_Joe_Biden "Inauguration of Joe Biden") . As of July 2026, Trump has made 12 international trips to 17 countries during [his second presidency](https://en.wikipedia.
org/wiki/Second_presidency_of_Donald_Trump "Second presidency of Donald Trump") , which began on [January 20, 2025](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_inauguration_of_Donald_Trump "Second inauguration of Donald Trump") .

Due to the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic") , he did not make any international trips between February 2020 and the end of his first presidency.

results.title: Chart: Trump's International Travels Mapped | Statista
excerpts:
The first Trump administration

U.S. President Donald Trump is headed to the United Kingdom for his second official state visit on Tuesday. Trump and the first lady are scheduled to meet with King Charles and Queen Camilla as well as UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer and other government officials. While Wednesday's visit to Windsor Castle will be including a lot of pomp and ceremony, Thursday's political meetings will be [circling around tariffs and a new technology partnership.](https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c4gw25w9841o/) Potentially due to his non-consecutive presidential terms, Trump will be the first non-royal in modern times to take part in two state visits to the UK. But the visit is also seen as Britain courting Trump in the context of the two countries' ongoing negotations around trade deals. Trump has visited the UK five times, more than any other country, [including in July](https://www.statista.
com/topics/13639/the-second-trump-administration/) when he also met with Keir Starmer as well as European Union President Ursula von der Leyen.

Trump has received an (inofficial) invitation from Russian President Vladimir Putin when the pair met in August in Alaska. Traveling to Russia was something Trump said he could see ["possibly happening".](https://www.axios.com/2025/08/16/trump-putin-moscow-ukraine-talks/)

Though unlikely, a visit to Russia would add another country to the list of official trips Trump has taken. He has visited several countries in Asia (compared to just one in Latin America) and paid many visits to European nations, including four visits to France and two each to Italy, Switzerland and Belgium. Germany, on the other hand, also a long-time U.S. ally, has only seen one Trump visit, for the G20 summit in Hamburg in 2017.
A bilateral visit with the German chancellor is still not on the agenda, which is highly unusual given the close cooperation of the two countries in the past. Trump has also stopped by at Ramstein airbase in South-West Germany in 2018, but this visit is not counted as a visit to German territory [by the State Department.](https://history.state.gov/departmenthistory/travels/president/trump-donald-j/)

Another country that Trump has frequented is Japan (two bilateral visits and one summit visit). The most unusual country that Trump has visited is certainly North Korea, which the president walked into for about a minute when meeting North Korean leader Kim Jong-un in the Korean Demilitarized Zone. No other sitting president had stepped foot in the country before, but the visit was not counted as such by the Office of the Historian at the State Department.

Katharina Buchholz

Data Journalist

On May 19, 2017, President Donald Trump departed Washington, D.C., for his first international trip as president. The trip lasted eight days and took Trump to five different countries.

animation%20%283%29.gif

## Contents

* 1 Saturday, May 20: Trump meets with Saudi Arabian leaders
* 2 Sunday, May 21: Trump delivers speech urging leaders of Muslim nations to join with the U.S. to fight extremism
* 3 Monday, May 22: Trump visits Israel and discusses anti-Iran coalition; becomes first sitting U.S. president to visit the Western Wall
  
    + 3\.1 Trump becomes first sitting U.S. president to visit the Western Wall

While in Israel, Trump met with President Reuven Rivlin, and he and first lady Melania Trump had dinner with Netanyahu and his wife, Sara Netanyahu. [[10]]() [[3]]()

According to _The New York Times_ , "No previous American president has come to Israel this early in his tenure. Bill Clinton visited in his second year in office and Jimmy Carter in his third, while Richard M. Nixon, George W. Bush and Barack Obama all waited until their second terms to make the trip." [[9]]()

#### Trump becomes first sitting U.S. president to visit the Western Wall

Trump became the first sitting U.S. president to visit the Western Wall in Jerusalem, the holiest site where Jews are allowed to pray. Trump rested his hand on the wall for a few moments and then placed a note inside of the wall. It is a tradition for worshippers to place slips of paper containing prayers to God in the cracks of the wall. First lady Melania Trump tucked a note into the wall, too.

### United Arab Emirates (May 15–16)

[ [edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=May_2025_visit_by_Donald_Trump_to_the_Middle_East&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: United Arab Emirates (May 15–16)") ]

Trump arrived in [Abu Dhabi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abu_Dhabi "Abu Dhabi") on May 15, becoming the second serving U.S. president to visit the country. [[ 38 ]]() He toured the [Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sheikh_Zayed_Grand_Mosque "Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque") with Khaled bin Mohamed Al Nahyan. [[ 39 ]]() The United Arab Emirates awarded Trump the [Order of Zayed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Order_of_Zayed "Order of Zayed") , the country's highest civil decoration.
